title: Spain vs Italy: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Spain and Italy based on Reddit discussions, real 2026 costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

categories.title: 💰 Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Spain is consistently cheaper than Italy, but the gap is smaller than many travelers expect — and highly location-dependent. Venice and the Amalfi Coast are genuinely expensive; southern Spain (Seville, Granada, Málaga) is remarkably affordable. Here's a real 2026 cost breakdown based on Numbeo data

categories.title: 🚆 Getting Around
categories.summary: Both countries have solid high-speed rail networks, but the experience differs significantly.

faqs.question: Is Spain or Italy better for first-time visitors to Europe?
faqs.answer: Both are excellent first-time Europe destinations with very different personalities. Italy wins on sheer historical weight — Rome, Florence, Venice, and the Amalfi Coast are bucket-list icons. Spain wins on lifestyle: the tapas culture is highly social, Barcelona's architecture is unlike anything el

faqs.question: Is Spain cheaper than Italy to visit?
faqs.answer: Yes, Spain is generally 10–20% cheaper for mid-range travelers. A good meal with wine typically costs €15–25/person in Spain vs €18–30 in Italy. faqs.question: Which has better food — Spain or Italy?
faqs.answer: Genuinely subjective. Italy has pasta, pizza, gelato, and one of the world's most refined regional culinary traditions. faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Spain vs Italy?
faqs.answer: For both countries, May–June and September–October are the sweet spots: warm weather, manageable crowds, and lower prices than peak summer. faqs.question: How many days do you need in Spain vs Italy?
faqs.answer: For a proper first visit to either country, plan 10–14 days minimum. Spain is geographically large and diverse — Madrid, Barcelona, Seville, Granada, and San Sebastián are all dramatically different. faqs.question: Can you visit both Spain and Italy on one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it's a natural combination. Budget airlines (Vueling, Ryanair, EasyJet) connect Spanish and Italian cities for €30–80 one way. faqs.question: Is Spain or Italy safer for tourists?
faqs.answer: Both are safe for tourists by global standards. The main concern in both countries is petty theft (pickpocketing) in tourist-heavy areas: Barcelona's La Rambla, Rome's Colosseum area, Naples, and Venice.
